chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a newborn who does not have what men have, nor does he have what women have.
He said: "The Imam casts lots for this one; he writes 'Abdullah (Slave of God)' on one lot, and writes 'Umdatullah (Slave of God)' on another lot.
Then the Imam or the one casting the lots says: 'O God, You are God, there is no god but You.
Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You judge between Your servants regarding that in which they differ.
Make clear the matter of this newborn for us, so that inheritance may be established for what You have prescribed for him in Your Book.
Then he throws the two lots into a container of indistinguishable lots, then they are shaken, and whichever comes out, inheritance is established upon it.'

key_terms.أَمَةَ اَللَّهِ: Umdatullah (Slave of God, used for female)
key_terms.عالِمَ اَلْغَيْبِ وَ اَلشَّهادَةِ: Knower of the unseen and the witnessed
key_terms.عَبْدَ اَللَّهِ: Abdullah (Slave of God, used for male)

ai.seo_question: How is the gender of a hermaphrodite determined for inheritance in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the juridical procedure for determining the inheritance gender of a hermaphrodite (Mukhannath) through lot-casting (Qur'ah) by the Imam. It highlights the Shia emphasis on divine guidance in legal ambiguity, where the Imam recites a supplication invoking Allah as the Judge between His servants before casting lots to assign either 'Abdullah' or 'Umdatullah' for inheritance purposes. This method ensures that the individual receives the fixed shares prescribed in the Quran, reflecting the scholarly tradition of using probabilistic legal tools when biological certainty is absent.
